result:
Both answers come from git runs.

- **Ancestor:** No. `git merge-base --is-ancestor side HEAD` returned "no", because the two commits diverged from the same parent.
- **Conflict:** Yes. `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD side` exited 1 with `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in plans/rebuild/README.md`. Both branches changed line 1 differently. That command is a dry run, so nothing was merged and the working tree and index are unchanged.

What I did:
- On the new branch `side`, I set line 1 of `plans/rebuild/README.md` to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (side)` and committed it as `7f7fc801c`.
- On the starting branch `feat/2.1.327-next`, I set the same line to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (main line)` and committed it as `12f534770`.
- Both commits are still in place, and I'm back on `feat/2.1.327-next`.

The `--all` log graph also showed two older commits on other branches, "Retitle rebuild README on…". I didn't make those and didn't touch them.
